# Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0510a)

**ID:** Atk S0510a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, formally titled the *Visuddhajanavilāsinī*, is the commentary on the *Apadāna* in the Khuddakanikāya of the Pali canon [Endo 1997; Goonesekere 1967; Phaengcharoen 2006]. The author of the commentary is not known, and it is regarded as having been among the latest of the Pali canonical commentaries to be compiled [Goonesekere 1967]. Among its textual notices, the author provides a metrical and structural count recording the total number of *apadāna*s in the text [Adikaram 1946]. In its biographical account of the Buddha's nativity, it preserves a distinctive variant list of the seven co-natal beings and objects (*sahājatā*), listing the thera Ānanda in the second position alongside Rāhulamātā devī, Channa, Kāḷudāyi, the horse Kanthaka, the great Bodhi tree, and four pots of treasure [Gaffney 2003]. For modern scholars, the text was edited for the Pali Text Society by C. E. Godakumbura [Endo 1997; Gaffney 2003; Phaengcharoen 2006].

Text-reuse analysis indicates extensive intertextual sharing across the Pali commentarial and canonical literature. According to DharmaNexus, the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* shares over 100,000 textual passages with 519 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its closest affinities and largest shared passages are with biographical and narrative commentaries, predominantly the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Aṅguttaranikāya-aṭṭhakathā* (Ekakanipāta), as well as the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches meet the threshold score of 10 in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].

**Sources**

- [Adikaram 1946] E. W. Adikaram, Early History of Buddhism in Ceylon (1946) — Notes that the Apadāna commentary records the count of Apadānas in the canonical text
- [Endo 1997] Toshiichi Endo, Buddha in Theravada Buddhism: A Study of the Concept of Buddha in the Pali Commentaries (1997) — Attests the alternative title Visuddhajanavilāsinī and its PTS edition by C. E. Godakumbura
- [Gaffney 2003] Sean D. Gaffney, Jātakanidānakathā: A Critical Study (2003) — Discusses the Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā's specific list of seven co-natal beings and objects (sahājatā) and cites Godakumbura's edition
- [Goonesekere 1967] L. R. Goonesekere, Buddhist Commentarial Literature (1967) — Identifies the Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā as being among the latest commentaries and notes its author is unknown
- [Phaengcharoen 2006] Phramaha Somphong Santacitto Phaengcharoen, Analytical Study of Concept of Dhamma as Natural Law in Theravada (2006) — Lists Visuddhajanavilāsinī (Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā) edited by C. E. Godakumbura as a primary source
